title: harmBounds
text: Stopping boundaries can calculated function getHarmBound. Let’s assume trial 10 safety interim analyses every 10 events (combined groups) total 100 events nominal test-wise alpha 0.025. data frame bounds specifies boundaries interim analysis, events_intervention minimal number events intervention group lead stopping trial. list stopprob contains stopping probability analysis null optionally alternative hypotheses (see ). Data frame opchar shows cumulative stopping probability expected number events hypothesis. example , overall Type error safety testing 7.2%. stop 100 total events (default, even boundary breached), expected number events 96. Typically, trial might stopped last interim analysis, can specified using maxevents option: like control Type error specific level (necessarily recommend, see ), test-wise alpha can obtained using function getAlphaPerTest. overall Type error 5.1%, .e. close 5% possible (given discrete nature test). Note example slightly higher 5%. strict control 5% required totalAlpha 0.049 chosen.

title: harmBounds
text: Stopping probabilities expected number events can obtained alternative scenarios getHarmBound function. alternative hypothesis can specified pH1: proportion events intervention group, 0.5 null scenario 1:1 rando, numbers 0.5 1 indicating safety problem. rrH1: risk ratio (intervention / control), 1 null scenario numbers >1 indicating safety problem. rdH1: risk difference (intervention minus control), 0 null scenario numbers >0 indicating safety problem. control proportion (r0) total number participants (n) specified. orH1: odds ratio (intervention / control), 1 null scenario number >1 indicating safety problem. control proportion (r0) specified. stay event-based setting, recommend using first two options (pH1 rrH1). Note stopprob now length two data frame condition. stop 7.2% trials null (safety problem) 59.2% alternative (safety problem 60% events intervention group). higher probability early stopping, expected number events reduced 142 H0 91 H1. (cumulative) stopping probabilities step can plotted using absstopPlot cumstopPlot (harmbound.plot-methods). now using one alternative make interesting:   can also specify vector alternatives plot cumulative stopping probabilities expected number events alternative.

code: alphaPerTest <- getAlphaPerTest(nevents = seq(10, 100, by = 10), pH0 = 0.5,   totalAlpha = 0.05) alist<-c(0.001,0.01,alphaPerTest,0.025,0.05)  hbl<-lapply(alist,function(x)   getHarmBound(nevents = seq(10, 100, by = 10), alpha_test = x,   pH0 = 0.5, pH1 = seq(0,1,l=100), maxevents = 150)$opchar)  hbd<-data.frame(do.call(rbind,hbl),alpha=rep(alist,each=nrow(hbl[[1]]))) hbd$alpha<-as.factor(round(hbd$alpha,4))  ggplot(hbd, aes(x = p, y = cum_stop_prob, colour=alpha)) +      geom_line() +     ylab("Stopping probability") +     xlab("Proportion of events in intervention group") +     scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.1),limits=c(0.2,0.8)) +     scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.2)) ggplot(hbd, aes(x = p, y = expected_events, colour=alpha)) +      geom_line() +     ylab("Expected number of events") +     xlab("Proportion of events in intervention group") +     scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.1),limits=c(0.2,0.8)) +     scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 150)) alphaPerTest <- getAlphaPerTest(nevents = seq(10, 100, by = 10), pH0 = 0.5,   totalAlpha = 0.05) alist<-c(0.001,0.01,alphaPerTest,0.025,0.05)  hbl<-lapply(alist,function(x)   getHarmBound(nevents = seq(10, 100, by = 10), alpha_test = x, pH0 = 0.5,   rrH1 = seq(0,10,l=100), maxevents = 150)$opchar)  hbd<-data.frame(do.call(rbind,hbl),alpha=rep(alist,each=nrow(hbl[[1]]))) hbd$alpha<-as.factor(round(hbd$alpha,4)) hbd$lrr<-log(hbd$rr)  ggplot(hbd, aes(x = rr, y = cum_stop_prob, colour=alpha)) +      geom_line() +     ylab("Stopping probability") +     xlab("Risk ratio (intervention/control)") +     scale_x_continuous(trans='log', breaks=c(0.5,0.75,1,1.5,2,3,4),       minor_breaks=NULL,limits=c(0.5,5)) +     scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.2))

title: harmBounds
text: number interim analyses impact steepness location curve, rather limited, long last interim analysis time point.  substantially decrease total error rates (.e. get steeper curves), need higher total number events:
code: nelist<-list(c(100),c(50,100),c(10,20,50,100),              seq(10, 100, by = 10),seq(10, 100, by = 1))  hbl<-lapply(nelist,function(x)   getHarmBound(nevents = x, alpha_test = 0.025, pH0 = 0.5,     pH1 = seq(0,1,l=100), maxevents = 150)$opchar)  nis<-unlist(lapply(nelist,length)) net<-unlist(lapply(nelist,function(x) paste(x,collapse = "/"))) net[[length(net)-1]]<-"every 10" net[[length(net)]]<-"continous" nism<-paste0(nis," (",net,")") hbd<-data.frame(do.call(rbind,hbl),ni=rep(nism,each=nrow(hbl[[1]]))) hbd$ni<-factor(hbd$ni,levels=nism)  ggplot(hbd, aes(x = p, y = cum_stop_prob, colour=ni)) +      geom_line() +     ylab("Stopping probability") +     xlab("Proportion of events in intervention group") +     scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.1),limits=c(0.2,0.8)) +     scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.2)) +     labs(colour="Number of IAs") nelist<-list(seq(10, 20, by = 10),seq(10, 50, by = 10), seq(10, 100, by = 10), seq(10, 200, by = 10))  hbl<-lapply(nelist,function(x)   getHarmBound(nevents = x, alpha_test = 0.025, pH0 = 0.5,   pH1 = seq(0,1,l=100))$opchar)  nis<-unlist(lapply(nelist,max)) hbd<-data.frame(do.call(rbind,hbl),ni=rep(nis,each=nrow(hbl[[1]]))) hbd$ni<-as.factor(hbd$ni)  ggplot(hbd, aes(x = p, y = cum_stop_prob, colour=ni)) +      geom_line() +     ylab("Stopping probability") +      xlab("Proportion of events in intervention group") +     scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.1),limits=c(0.2,0.8)) +     scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.2)) +     labs(colour="Total number of events")

title: Harm boundaries for safety testing — getHarmBound
text: nevents vector number events (arms) interim analysis done alpha_test nominal alpha level use test pH0 proportion events intervention arm null hypothesis, typically based randomization ratio (e.g. 0.5 1:1 randomization) maxevents optional maximum number events expected trial (arms), used calculate expected number events pH1 optional alternative, numeric vector, proportion events intervention arm rrH1 alternative specification alternative risk ratio (intervention / control) orH1 alternative specification alternative risk ratio (intervention / control). Requires control proportion (r0). rdH1 alternative specification alternative risk difference (intervention - control). Requires control proportion (r0) number participants (n). r0 risk control group. Required alternative given risk difference odds ratio. n total number participants. Required alternative given risk difference.

title: Harm boundaries for safety testing — getHarmBound
text: list 3 data.frames: bounds, stopprob opchar. bounds row interim analysis columns number events (events), number events control intervention group lead stop (events_intervention, events_control), nominal alpha test (alpha_test). stopprob row interim analysis columns number events (events), hypothesis (pH), stopping probability (stop_prob), cumulative stopping probability (cum_stop_prob) opchar row hypothesis (null plus alternative) columns assumed proportion events intervention group (p), cumulative stopping probabilities (cum_stop_prob) expected total number events (expected_events) null alternative.
